title: Mech radio-chatter audio system (ElevenLabs + spatial/proximity)
summary: ElevenLabs-generated ATC-style radio chatter per mech/pilot, triggered on pilot assignment/turn start/damage/crit/crit-fail, run through a radio-compression effect that degrades further as the mech takes damage, bookended by consistent beeps; proximity-based ambient volume for enemies on both the campaign map and smaller battle maps.
description:
A custom ElevenLabs API integration to generate unique radio-chatter lines per mech and (once named) per pilot. Explicitly scoped down: NOT for every scene, NOT full character dialogue — background flavor audio tied specifically to mech-relevant events, to bring pilots/Frames into the world without becoming a full voice-acting system. Trigger points named: when a pilot is assigned to a mech, when it becomes their turn in initiative, on taking damage, on landing a critical hit, on suffering a critical failure.

Processing: run the generated lines through effects that make them sound like compressed radio/walkie-talkie chatter rather than clean AI voice — 'the closer it sounds to a handheld walkie talkie noise the better.' Additionally, the chatter should audibly degrade/break up more as the mech takes damage — audio quality as a diegetic readout of the Frame's condition. Needs a consistent bookending SFX (start/end 'beep,' like a push-to-talk button) and its own constructed in-fiction ATC-style lingo/vocabulary for mech pilot radio communication.

Spatial extension: enemies (Claimants/Frames) as audio sources — as players move closer to an enemy on the campaign-scale map, the sounds of battle get louder automatically. A similar effect is wanted at smaller battle-map scale (alien idle noises intensifying with proximity to enemy tokens).

Related existing assets: audio/in-tray/dialogue/control/ already has one real ElevenLabs-generated test line (voice preset 'Juniper - Grounded and Professional'), confirming this is already in motion, not purely speculative.

**2026-09-17 — the audio substrate this needs now exists** (`design/audio-system.md`): a `voice` kind normalised for radio traffic, one-shot broadcast to every client with ducking, and 'scatter' layers that fire a random clip from a set every N seconds (already carrying 65 real dispatch/ATC/SWAT clips). What this idea still needs on top: ElevenLabs generation per pilot, the radio-degradation-by-damage effect, the push-to-talk bookends, and proximity. None of that is built; the plumbing under it is.
sourceContext: User planning message, 2026-08-22 — large worldbuilding/tooling brain-dump.
openSubQuestions: The actual ATC-lingo vocabulary/glossary for mech pilot radio comms — not designed yet.
Exact trigger-to-audio mapping and how many line variants per trigger to avoid repetition fatigue.
Technical approach for the radio-compression/degradation effect (real-time DSP vs. pre-rendered variants per damage state).
Technical approach for proximity-based volume on both the campaign map and battle maps — likely connects to whatever the in-scene overlay/UI system ends up being.
